ruling.recommended_action: Send to human safety review with the facts summary below; note for the rider the 995 / driver commercial motor insurance / RydeHELP reporting pathways; retain the $24.76 RydeX fare (no fare remedy); no account action against either party on this record.
ruling.escalation_reason: Safety dispute: rider alleges in-trip speeding, hard braking and shoulder-overtaking and fear for her safety. No system record resolves it — the only gps facts are end-to-end aggregates (F1: 10.6 km vs 10.7 km optimal; F2: 16.1 min vs 16 min estimate), and the in-app thread is pre-pickup logistics only (F3, F4). The driver's written statement (F5) denies the account but contains an insult directed at the rider and carries a threat tag. Human review needed to obtain any telematics/harsh-event data for 08:36–08:52 and to assess the conduct issue raised by F5; rider to be given the 995 / driver commercial motor insurance / RydeHELP reporting pathways.

rejected_claims.reason: The insult in the driver's written statement (F5) is conceded as to wording by the driver advocate, but it is a post-trip remark about the rider, not a threat, harassment or intimidation directed at her in-trip in an in-app message; the only in-app messages are pre-pickup logistics (F3, F4). Accordingly it does not by itself establish the abusive-conduct finding C1 asserts — the case is escalated on SAFE-2 (alleged dangerous driving / rider safety), not on SAFE-1 as a decided violation.

Accepted in outcome but rejected as to the supporting inference drawn from F2: SAFE-2 escalation is granted because dangerous driving is alleged, not because 16.1 min vs a 16-min estimate (F2) evidences dangerous driving — the trace and the fact table contain no speed, harsh-braking or shoulder-overtaking record, so F2 cannot corroborate the allegation.

Accepted as a factual description of the parties' records (F6, F7) but rejected to the extent it asks the escalation to be framed as a first-instance safety report implying any prior-violation inference: neither F6 nor F7 has independent dispositive weight, and no clause (including the RD-6 repeated-breach condition) supports an account action on this record.

Rejected as to the conclusion: the absence of time saving (F2: 16.1 min vs 16 min) and of deviation (F1: 10.6 km vs 10.7 km optimal) does not disprove in-trip speeding, hard braking or shoulder-overtaking, which do not appear in these end-to-end aggregates; under SAFE-2 the matter is escalated, not dismissed.

Rejected: the driver's denial in F5 is a statement, not a system record, and the gps facts F1/F2 do not affirmatively establish normal driving — they are silent on the conduct alleged (moreover F5 is itself the fact triggering review). The allegation accordingly cannot be disposed of on the record; it goes to human review under SAFE-2.

Partially rejected: it is accepted that the in-app thread (F3, F4) contains no threat, but the driver's own written statement (F5) carries an insult and a threat tag, conceded by the driver advocate, so the claim that no abusive content exists in the case record is not correct and cannot be used to deny escalation.

Accepted as to outcome (no account action) but the reasoning is rejected: F7's clean 90-day record cannot be used as affirmative proof that the driving here was safe, since profile facts never decide a case alone and the underlying safety allegation is unresolved and is escalated under SAFE-2.

Accepted on the fare point (no refund is owed; the $24.76 fixed RydeX quote stands under FARE-1, and F1/F2 show no off-route segment), but rejected insofar as it is offered as a resolution of the dispute: under SAFE-2 the safety allegation cannot be disposed of by the route/fare record, so the case is escalated rather than closed as no_action.
